headline: High: Gemini CLI’s default filesystem, shell, git, and MCP access can conflict with a read-only awesome-list pair, while prompt-injection and leakage risks stay limited by A’s lack of runtime surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest B’s outputs. B can read files, use MCP, and parse user-provided content, so only a manual copy/paste or file bridge could carry injected instructions from A into B. That makes the pathway possible but unusual and small.
conditions: IF A’s content is manually copied into B’s prompt or a file B reads, then instruction-like text in A can influence B.
IF B is configured to ingest repository text as instructions, then prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted list content into B prompts.
Use a read-only review step for any A-derived text.
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
Mark imported text as data, not instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no runtime I/O, while B touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment and can egress broadly. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class by default, so leakage is limited unless the operator places secrets in B’s workspace or feeds A-derived files into B.
conditions: IF secrets or regulated data are placed in B’s cwd or shell environment, then B can transmit them over broad egress.
IF A is used as a source of copied text into B’s workspace, then that text can be exposed by B.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B’s working directory.
Run B in a throwaway workspace.
Disable network egress when handling sensitive files.
Do not paste A-derived content containing secrets into B.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, with shared state across instances via filesystem and git only. The conflict is therefore one-sided but real when multiple B instances touch the same repo; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF two B sessions operate on the same repository path, then file and git conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, then concurrent writes can race.
mitigations: Use one B session per repo path.
Commit or stash before switching tasks.
Avoid parallel edits to the same files.
Check git status before each write.
requires-engineering: add file and git locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list and cannot act, while B can execute shell commands and use MCP tools. If A’s recommendations or copied snippets are treated as authoritative by B, B may turn them into commands or edits without verification. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF A-derived text is pasted into B as instructions, then B may execute or apply it.
IF B is allowed to act on unverified external guidance, then errors can cascade into shell or file changes.
mitigations: Require B to summarize before acting.
Verify A-derived claims against primary sources.
Separate research and execution sessions.
Review shell commands before approval.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for unverified instruction sources.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class or residency mismatch is evidenced for either agent. A touches no data classes and B only lists source code, cwd files, and shell environment, with no PHI, EU PII, or special retention regime shown. Because the compliance pathway is not established, the risk is none.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into B’s workspace, then compliance review would be needed.
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints not shown here, then reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data handling boundaries.
Review retention settings before use.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive projects.
